newsitem.title: ITALY: DeBenedetti to plea bargain in insider trade probe.
newsitem.headline: DeBenedetti to plea bargain in insider trade probe.

text.p: Former Olivetti head Carlo De Benedetti has asked to plea bargain in preliminary court proceedings against him for alleged insider trading, a spokesman for his industrial holding CIR said on Wednesday.
The former chairman of the information technology group has been under investigation by Turin magistrates for alleged insider trading in Olivetti's shares last August.
The CIR spokesman said De Benedetti, who remains honorary chairman of Olivetti, was sure investigations against him by stock market watchdog Consob were unfounded.
But the spokesman said De Benedetti "prefers to agree to pay a financial penalty to avoid the damage to his reputation and the cost to CIR which would inevitably result from a judicial prosecution".
"Consenting to plea bargain does not constitute admission of responsibility," the spokesman added.

The magistrate presiding over the preliminary hearing in Turin, which is close to Olivetti's headquarters at Ivrea in northwest Italy, will decide in the coming weeks whether to grant the plea bargain request.

The trading period in question is August 1996, a month before the publication of Olivetti's half-year accounts, which showed further losses at the struggling group, and De Benedetti's sudden resignation as chairman.
The flamboyant entrepreneur was quizzed for four hours by Turin magistrates in December and at the time said he had demonstrated "the total lack of substance behind the insider trading theory".
Last autumn's boardroom convulsions, which eventually resulted in the appointment of Roberto Colaninno as chief executive, also prompted another investigation into the group's accounts.
A senior manager resigned in September over the publication of the first-half results, saying he did not agree with all the figures in the report. That investigation is still under way.
